newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BECKHAM CAN LEARN FROM ZOLA ROLLER-COASTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BECKHAM CAN LEARN FROM ZOLA ROLLER-COASTER.

text.p: Gianfranco Zola and David Beckham are a generation apart and have contrasting styles but look set to be the key figures when Chelsea play Manchester United in England's top league game this weekend.

It is less than two years since Beckham, still only 21, made his full league debut for United but he has developed into an integral part of Alex Ferguson's talented midfield as well as an automatic choice for England.
He has also developed a reputation for scoring fantastic long range goals and has confidence way beyond his years.
Everything is coming up roses for Beckham, as it is for 30-year-old Zola, but the Italian, more than anyone, can warn his younger rival about the potholes along the road to football's Hall of Fame.
Zola is currently the darling of Chelsea and Italy, but his journey to the top has been studded with disappointments which might have crushed a lesser man.
A late developer, he was signed by Napoli at the age of 23 and served as understudy to Diego Maradona as the southern Italian side won the Serie A title.
"At first I was intimidated to be at the same club as Maradona," Zola said. "But he was good to me and I learnt so much about the game from him."
After four seasons at Napoli he moved to Parma where he scored an impressive 49 goals in 102 league games, many with free kicks he learned from the Argentine World Cup winner.
His goals helped Parma to their second successive European Cup Winners' Cup final in 1994, although Arsenal prevented a second title.
His performances had marked him as one of the world's leading attacking midfielders and he would have been an automatic choice in most national teams.
But Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi was adamant his line-up could not accommodate both Zola and Roberto Baggio - and it was the Parma man who missed out.
As Italy spluttered through the 1994 World Cup, Zola had to watch from the bench,.
He finally got his chance as a substitute against Nigeria, only to be sent off for "stamping" after just 12 minutes on the pitch in one of the harshest decisions in the history of the tournament.
Zola could only watch as Baggio went on to save Italy - and then turn villain by missing a penalty in the final shoot-out.
Finally, as Baggio lost form the following season, Sacchi turned to the Parma man.

Things began to go well again as Zola helped Parma to the UEFA Cup in 1995 and became Italy's fulcrum for the 1996 European Championships, only to miss a penalty against old rivals Germany as his country crashed out in the qualifying stages.

Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti caused him further angst by forcing him to play wide midfield before salvation arrived in the form of a move to Chelsea, where his coruscating dribbling made him an instant favourite.
He followed a superb performance against Liverpool in the F.A. Cup by scoring the only goal as Italy beat England in a vital World Cup qualifier at Wembley.
"Zola Genius" screamed the front page of Italy's Tuttosport newspaper as once again his star was in the ascendancy.
While the compact Zola is clearly built on the Maradona model, Beckham appears to be on the way to filling the boots of former United and England hero Bobby Charlton.
Driving midfield running, pinpoint passing and devastating shooting mark Beckham as a natural successor to Charlton - and even the great man himself never scored from beyond the half-way line.
That amazing goal by Beckham on the opening day of the season, followed by superb long range goals against Tottenham, are a mark of his absolute confidence.
But as United fans look ever more to him to lead the way, he is not getting carried away with all the adulation.
"I don't take anything for granted," he said. Things can change so quickly." Zola would agree to that.
